author: Swinhoe, 1863
status: 나그네새, 해마다 수백 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)

months.note: 남한에서는 이동 시기에만 보이고, 백두산 고지대에서는 여름에 번식한다.

summary: 남한에서는 이동 시기에만 볼 수 있는 희귀한 나그네새이고, 여름에는 백두산 고지대에서 작은 무리가 번식한다. 숲속에서 지내며 곤충을 주로 먹는다. 국외에서는 러시아, 중국, 일본, 동남아시아에 분포한다.

sexes.male: 머리꼭대기·뒷목·작은날개덮깃이 파랗고 등·날개·꼬리는 검으며, 턱 아래는 희고 뺨·배·허리는 적갈색이다. 부리는 갈색 띤 검은색이다.
sexes.female: 머리·등·꼬리가 회갈색이고 턱 아래·가슴·배는 흰색이다. 부리는 갈색이고 기부는 엷다.

art.subject: White-throated Rock Thrush (Monticola gularis), adult male on spring passage (May): crown and nape bright cobalt-blue; black lores and ear coverts forming a dark mask; mantle and back black; wings black with a bright blue patch on the lesser coverts and a clear white patch on the wing; rump, breast, belly and flanks rich chestnut-orange; a sharply defined white patch on the chin and centre of the throat, framed by chestnut on the lower cheeks and neck sides; tail dark blackish-blue; bill brownish-black; dark eye; brownish flesh-coloured legs.
art.pose: perched on a branch inside the forest, side view
art.scene: Korean forest interior during spring migration; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view perched upright: cobalt-blue crown and nape, black mask through the eye, white throat patch, chestnut lower cheeks, breast, belly and rump, black back and tail, wings with a blue shoulder and a white patch, brownish-flesh legs

adult female, side view perched: grey-brown upperparts scaled with dark crescents, white throat bordered by a dark malar stripe, buffy-white breast and belly densely scaled with dark crescents, brown bill with a paler base
art.build: Small rock thrush, noticeably larger than a sparrow and a little smaller than Blue Rock Thrush (Monticola solitarius); compact, with a rounded head and short square tail. Sits quietly upright on shaded branches inside the forest, often motionless for long spells. Bill straight and slender, about two-thirds of the head length. Legs fairly short, brownish flesh. In flight the white wing patch flashes on the dark wing.
avoid: Do not paint a blue throat and breast — that is Blue Rock Thrush (Monticola solitarius); here the throat is white and the breast chestnut.
Do not paint the whole face chestnut; the lores and ear coverts form a black mask.
Do not give the male a blue back; only the crown, nape and shoulder are blue.
Do not paint the female plain and unmarked; her upperparts and underparts are densely scaled.
